question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{gcd}(321,213)=3$

II. $\text{gcd}(321,213)=1$

III. $321$ and $213$ are coprime
question.worked_solution:
Recall that two integers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is $1.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. Indeed, let's use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}321 & = & 213\cdot 1 & + & 108 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 213 & = & 108\cdot 1 & + & 105 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 108 & = & 105\cdot 1 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 105 & = & 3\cdot 35 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The last positive remainder is $3.$ So, the greatest common divisor of $321$ and $213$ is $3:$

$$
\text{gcd}(321,213)=3.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $\text{gcd}(321,213)>1,$ the numbers are not coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
